clusters.label: DDR_ECC
clusters.representative_signature: DDR_ECC | DDR: ECC uncorrectable error ; FW: Memtest mismatch ; DDR: DDR PHY register snapshot ; SYSTEM: DDR subsystem failure ; DDR: ECC corrected errors rising ; DDR: CDC synchronizer glitch ; DDR: Read retry invoked

hypotheses.root_cause: A clock-domain-crossing synchroniser glitch in the DDR controller read FIFO (phy->ctrl) on ch1 corrupted read data, leading to a rising corrected-ECC rate, read retries, and then an uncorrectable ECC error and memtest mismatch.
hypotheses.rationale: Before the failure there are no WARN or ERROR lines at all from 0 to 8000 ms. Then the usual DDR_ECC sequence plays out on ch1: corrected ECC errors rising on bank 6 (8503 ms), a read retry (8621 ms), an uncorrectable error (8855 ms), a memtest mismatch (8910 ms), and the fatal error at 2400 MHz. The one warning that points to a specific cause is 'CDC synchronizer glitch | fifo=rd_fifo domain=phy->ctrl' at 8526 ms, which matches the catalogue tell-tale for RC_DDR_CDC_GLITCH, and it lands right as the errors start climbing. I found none of the markers for the other causes: no timing parameter violation (tRFC/tRCD), no low training margin, and no VDDQ droop (only VCORE is logged, with droop_cnt=0). The top historical match (run 000016, timing violation) is only similar because it has the same generic DDR_ECC signature. Its distinguishing marker is missing here, so I'm giving it less weight. The PHY register dump has no labels, so I couldn't read anything from it. Confidence is moderate because this rests on a single warning line and the cause has only been seen once in the corpus.
recommended_actions: Review the CDC constraints and synchroniser design (number of synchroniser stages, gray-coded pointers) on the rd_fifo between PHY and controller, and check STA/CDC lint reports for that boundary
Reproduce at corner voltage/temperature and at 2400 MHz vs a lower DRAM frequency to see whether the glitch and ECC errors track the clock ratio rather than DRAM timings
Add a monitor that counts rd_fifo CDC glitches and timestamp it against corrected ECC events on ch1 bank 6 to confirm they are causally linked
As a check against the alternative, re-run with relaxed tRCD/tRFC: if the failure persists unchanged, a timing violation (RC_DDR_TIMING_VIOLATION) is effectively ruled out

trace.output:
Prior for DDR_ECC: DDR uncorrectable ECC error following rising corrected-error rate
Corrected ECC errors trending up, then a read-retry, then an uncorrectable error and memtest mismatch indicate a marginal DRAM timing/training edge, often aggravated by voltage droop under load.

- RC_DDR_TIMING_VIOLATION: A DRAM timing parameter is violated at the configured frequency
    tell-tales: timing parameter violation, trfc, trcd
    actions: Relax the flagged timing parameter and re-run the memtest; Cross-check the DRAM datasheet timings against the controller config
- RC_DDR_TRAINING_EDGE: Read/write training converged on a marginal edge
    tell-tales: read training margin low, margin_ps
    actions: Re-run training with per-bit deskew and widen the margin window; Sweep VREF to re-centre the data eye
- RC_PMU_DROOP_UNDER_LOAD: VDDQ droop under load corrupts DRAM accesses
    tell-tales: fast droop event, rail=vddq
    actions: Correlate the UE with the VDDQ droop and add decoupling on the rail; Tune the regulator transient response for the memory rail
- RC_DDR_CDC_GLITCH: Clock-domain-crossing synchroniser glitch in the controller
    tell-tales: cdc synchronizer glitch, cdc
    actions: Review CDC constraints on the controller/PHY boundary; Reproduce at corner voltage/frequency to isolate the glitch
